case_title: A Prakash v. State of Rajasthan
aggravating_circumstances: Enmity between complainant and accused, threat given by accused to finish the family of complainant
trial_court_outcome: Convicted and sentenced to life imprisonment
neutral_facts: The minor son of the complainant left for school on the morning of the incident but did not return. His body was found several hours later on a hill. The investigation led to the arrest of three accused individuals for offenses punishable under Sections 302, 364, and 120-B of the Indian Penal Code. The prosecution relied on circumstantial evidence, including the last seen theory, recovery of incriminating articles, and the presence of motive. Witnesses testified that the accused were seen with the child on a scooter, and the accused had a history of enmity with the complainant. The prosecution also presented forensic evidence showing bloodstains on clothing recovered from the accused's home. The trial court convicted the accused and sentenced them to life imprisonment, which was affirmed by the High Court.
